//coverImage: The manuscript ships no cover photograph — only a portrait TOPIC 2 infographic on a cream ground, which cannot sit in the landscape hero window without being cut, and which left broad empty cream bands when it was padded to fit. So the hero is built rather than fitted: four of the manuscript’s own pictures as a full-bleed 2x2 mosaic at exactly 2474x1340 = the window’s 144:78 at 436 DPI for its 144mm printed width, so the pictures reach all four edges and the engine crops nothing. The four are chosen for what they show as well as for quality: between them they carry a wheelchair user, an albino learner and a blind man with a white cane, and the people counted across all four are close to evenly male and female (house rule: every picture with people in it, the cover included). Each cell keeps a 144:78 band chosen so no face is cut; the ambitions picture is additionally cropped past its lettered chalkboard and above its DREAM PLAN card, because a cover carries no half-read lettering. At the centre is Zambia — the outline traced from the Geography Form 1 book’s population map (the border only, none of that map’s labels, colours or legend) in the theme’s gold on its indigo, ringed by the four religions the RE syllabus teaches: the cross, the star and crescent, om and the Baha’i nine-pointed star. OUTSTANDING: the four photographs are not themselves religious. The manuscript contains no picture of worship, scripture or religious life in any of the four religions — its 18 pictures are lettered infographics about forgiveness, justice, ethics and hope plus these four scenes — so a cover whose PICTURES depict the subject needs new artwork generated (see docs/HOUSE-STYLE.md §5 on gpt-image-2).

//subtext: Round 2. Two standardisations the proofreader asked for and one spelling. (1) The line introducing each Specific Competence was written four different ways across the book's 22 sub-topics - 'In this sub-topic, you will:' 12 times, 'In this subtopic, you will:' 4, 'In this subtopic, you will learn to:' 4, 'In this sub-topic, you will learn to:' once, 'In this section, you will:' once. The notes 'let it be sub-topic' (page 2) and 'make this standard for all before the specific competences' (page 75) both point at it, so all 22 are normalised to the commonest form. The two other 'In this section, you will ...' sentences are running prose, not lead-ins, and are left alone. (2) 'rumors' -> 'rumours': the note reads 'delete and write like this; rumuors', which is a slip for the British spelling - the book already writes 'rumours' twice against 'rumors' twice, and is consistently -our/-ise throughout (behaviour 55, colour 48, recognise 31, and no American spelling anywhere). (4) The second author's name was printed three ways in one book: 'Mirriam Mhone Muzona' on the cover (set by the authors override, on her own instruction), 'Mirriam Mhone-Muzona' on the imprint page, and 'Mirriam Mhone\u2011Muzona' - with a non-breaking hyphen - in her own AUTHORS biography. The instruction had only ever reached the cover. Both hyphenated forms are now normalised to the spelling she asked for. (5) Spelling found at the pre-print check, none of it raised by the proofreader. The book is consistently British - behaviour 55, colour 48, recognise 31, organis- 26, apologis- 16 - but carried one 'apologize', one 'organizations', and used the American 'practicing/practice' for the VERB in four places against nine British 'practising'. The noun 'into practice' is correct and is left alone. The sentence ending '...the relationship between freedom and laws in the community' had no full stop, in both places it appears. CDC round (25 Oct 2026), printed pages 43, 80, 124 and 130 of the CDC copy: "The word 'sub-topic' should be deleted as it is not a subtopic but a competence (In this section, you will:". Those four are the Specific Competence lead-ins that sit in the MIDDLE of a sub-topic (after an exercise), not under a sub-topic heading. The book has five such; the fifth (2.5.1.2) is the one the manuscript itself typed 'In this section, you will:', so the old mapping that turned it into 'sub-topic' is dropped and all five now read 'In this section, you will:'. The seventeen lead-ins directly under a sub-topic heading keep 'In this sub-topic, you will:' (round 2's 'let it be sub-topic'). Spelling sweep (CDC round): favoritism -> favouritism (the book also writes favouritism), favoring -> favouring, quarreled -> quarrelled - British spelling, as the rest of the book.

(1) Bhagavad Gita 3:8 was the only scriptural reference for Hinduism anywhere in the sub-topic - the Hindu prose cites none, while Christianity carries five references, Islam carries Qur'an 53:39 and Zambian Traditional Religion carries proverbs. insertText.text: Dharma – One’s duty or responsibility to live rightly in Hinduism.
Division – The separation of people into opposing groups because of disagreements, prejudice, selfish interests or differences.
Hatred – A strong feeling of dislike, hostility or bitterness towards another person or group.
Nepotism – Giving unfair advantages or opportunities to relatives instead of selecting people fairly according to their abilities.
Penance – Taking action to correct or make amends for a wrong that has been committed.

insertText.before: Restorative justice – A form of justice
insertText.text: Repentance – Recognising that one has done wrong, feeling sorry and deciding to change.
Sin – Any thought, word or action that goes against God’s will or accepted moral values.
